synthetic_plan.tone_selection: Nearest original grid points to 1 kHz, 16 kHz folded image and separately 18 kHz legitimate host baseband; prospectively frozen.
synthetic_plan.bypass: 31-internal-sample unit delay, compared with the same correct-production-FIR baseband reference. Native-minus-double includes intentional filter corruption, not just arithmetic.
synthetic_plan.interpretation: Clean low and 18 kHz baseband pass. Above-Nyquist high/mixed through the stock FIR and deliberate bypass fail the same rails. This detects actual synthetic folding and exposes finite stock stopband rejection, not a universal 150 dB promise.

capture_witness.method: Actual public process(...,1), then the existing friend reads the last two decimator history entries; no copied feedback/FIFO/render scheduler or production hook.
capture_witness.validation: Require prepared, linked 2:1, eight active voices, post-call not-idle, finite input and exact cursor+2. The pre-call idle flag may still reflect reset before the first actual render.

limits: The old total-signal cap remains failed for the ON experiment; no readiness waiver or production test substitution occurred.
This measures only output-decimator contamination. Internal baseband may already contain upstream nonlinear alias, numerical content or modeled noise; existing independent guards remain untouched.
Finite-window B/I can contain window leakage. Tiny cancellation-scale image values are not resolved physical-alias evidence.

The stock 63-tap FIR gives roughly 75 dB stopband design and about 80 dB at the synthetic high tone. The 150 dB/-180 dBFS rails depend on the fixed fixture/input envelope, not arbitrary out-of-band inputs.
Tone, physical-source correctness, natural repicks/note changes and realtime readiness need independent qualification. Candidate95 failed absolute-tone qualification.
Ignored binaries, raw traces and full per-frequency arrays are not product inputs or shipped audio. This public record contains compact results and their frozen hashes.
